question.problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the subspace spanned by $a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

In our case, $A=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =(29)^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{29}[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 & 8 \\ -6 & 9 & -12 \\ 8 & -12 & 16\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
